categories.title: Categories to track
categories.description: Category slugs ("electronics", "toys-and-games"), sub-category node paths ("electronics/172541"), or full Amazon list URLs. A full URL overrides the marketplace and list type below, so one run can mix marketplaces.

listType.title: List type
listType.description: Which ranked list to track. Use 'bestsellers' and let this actor compute the movers - Amazon's own Movers & Shakers pages returned no data in every category tested (see the README).

maxRank.title: Max rank
maxRank.description: How deep to track. Amazon serves 50 ranks per page and stops at 100, so 100 is the maximum and costs two requests per category.

trackMovement.title: Track rank movement between runs
trackMovement.description: Compare each run against the previous one and label every product NEW_ENTRY, RISING, FALLING, UNCHANGED or DROPPED_OUT, with the exact rank change. This is what turns the actor into a Movers & Shakers tracker; the snapshot lives in a named key-value store so it survives scheduled runs.

onlyMovers.title: Only output movers
onlyMovers.description: Emit only products that moved significantly (5+ ranks), entered the list, or dropped out - the shortlist for winning-product research. On the very first run everything counts as NEW_ENTRY because there is nothing to compare against yet.

includeDroppedOut.title: Include dropped-out products
includeDroppedOut.description: Emit a row for products that were ranked last run and are not any more. Only visible by diffing snapshots, and a useful signal in its own right.

stateStoreName.title: State store name
stateStoreName.description: Named key-value store holding the previous run's ranks. Use different names to track separate watchlists independently.

delaySeconds.title: Delay between requests (seconds)
delaySeconds.description: Pause between page fetches. Amazon serves a CAPTCHA to traffic it dislikes, and this actor never solves CAPTCHAs - pacing is what keeps a run clean.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Recommended for scheduled runs. Amazon serves CAPTCHAs to datacentre IPs it dislikes; a residential proxy plus the built-in fingerprint rotation avoids them.
